title: Network layers: where is it broken?
summary: "The network is down" says nothing. The OSI layers sort a failure by where it happens, from the cable to the application.

text: The OSI model cuts a network into 7 layers. Each one relies on the one below and serves the one above.
- It's a way to reason, not the real Internet: that runs on TCP/IP, which merges some layers.
- Don't learn the names by heart. Learn which layer a symptom points to: that tells you where to look.

scheme: IP works, the name fails      DNS (7)
text: Start from the failure and find its layer.
- Refused: the machine answered (layers 1 to 3 work), usually nothing listens on that port, sometimes a firewall rule rejects it.
- An HTTP 500 means everything below worked: the bug is in the application itself.
- The name fails but the address works: the network is fine, DNS isn't.

scheme: curl https://… works: the machine is up
text: A failing test only proves something about its own layer.
- ping uses ICMP. Many firewalls block it: no answer doesn't prove the server is off.
- A test that succeeds higher up (a page loads) proves every layer below works.
- The Network path climbs these layers one command at a time: when the network breaks, a ladder.
